rules.rationale: Source ESOL prior gives smiles_short a positive effect (+6.89); small solutes solvate readily.
Source prior for smiles_mid is negative (-6.61); added nonpolar surface costs solvation free energy.
Ring role carried the largest transfer weight (0.76); acyclic solutes lack rigid hydrophobic ring surface.
Rotatable-bond role maps to branching (transfer weight 0.76); minimal branching reduces buried nonpolar volume.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers signed ESOL size priors plus ring and branching roles to FreeSolv, assuming solubility and hydration share size-driven mechanisms. Fails if hydration is dominated by polarity rather than molecular size.

rules.rationale: Hydration free energy is dominated by polar N/O hydrogen bonding with water, not chain length.
Hydrocarbon-only solutes incur hydrophobic cavity-formation cost and poor water hydrogen bonding.
Heavy halogenation raises nonpolar surface and lowers water affinity despite modest polarizability.
Counter to low-confidence ESOL length prior (0.28); many short candidates are nonpolar alkanes.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the weak ESOL length prior and asserts heteroatom polarity drives hydration affinity. Fails if the score rewards nonpolar compactness or if hetero_high (28 candidates) is too sparse to inform the surrogate.

fixed_initial.lesson: Source ESOL role confidences were low (0.16-0.41) and the size prior was weakest; hydration free energy is mechanistically a polarity phenomenon, so a polarity-led counter-hypothesis with fast semantic decay is safer than direct size transfer.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept a faithful source-grounded transfer using the signed smiles_length priors plus the high-weight ring and branch roles, and added a counter-hypothesis that downweights the low-confidence short-length prior in favor of heteroatom polarity and halogen hydrophobicity. Both skills use only catalog field-value pairs, decay semantic mass toward the target-only anchor, and the polarity skill was frozen for deployment.

rules.rationale: Dense N/O centers donate and accept water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable hydration free-energy term.
Apolar solutes pay cavity-formation cost with no compensating solute-water hydrogen bonding.
Source ring role had the highest transfer weight (0.76); acyclic solutes expose less rigid hydrophobic ring surface.
Dense halogenation increases nonpolar surface area and weakens water affinity despite added polarizability.

skills.hypothesis: Combines the polarity contrast that led generation 0 with the source-grounded acyclic ring role that led generation 1, plus a halogen penalty. Fails if scaffold shape is redundant once polarity is modeled.

rules.rationale: Phenol- and aniline-like substituted aromatics hydrate strongly, contradicting a blanket penalty on ring-containing solutes.
Multiple polar centers retain the mechanistically central hydrogen-bonding advantage in aqueous solvation.
Pure hydrocarbons remain the hydrophobic tail of the hydration distribution.
Broad halogen-free set (467) avoids the nonpolar surface penalty of perhalogenated solutes.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis: reverses the uncertain source ring role by rewarding polar-substituted aromatics instead of acyclic scaffolds. Fails if ring surface truly dominates and aromatic_low is chemically heterogeneous.

true_feedback.lesson: Across both development generations, heteroatom polarity was the consistently useful prior, while the pure size/length transfer was weakest; the polarity-plus-scaffold hybrid scored highest in generation 1, but seed variance was large, so the hybrid is adopted cautiously with fast decay to the target-only anchor.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Merged the two best development configurations into one deployed skill: the polarity contrast (hetero_high positive, hetero_none negative) from the generation-0 leader plus the source-grounded acyclic ring role and halogen penalty from the generation-1 leader, dropping the hetero_mid rule that coincided with the weaker generation-1 core run. The second skill is a fresh counter-hypothesis that reverses the uncertain ring transfer by rewarding polar-substituted aromatics via a single chemically meaningful two-condition interaction. All conditions use exact catalog field-value pairs, semantic mass decays toward the target-only anchor, and no target outcomes are claimed.

rules.rationale: Dense N/O centers form multiple water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Moderate heteroatom content still supplies polar solvation and covers 91 candidates for surrogate stability.
Unsubstituted hydrocarbons offer no hydrogen-bond partners and pay full hydrophobic cavity cost.

skills.hypothesis: Downweights the weakest source role (length, confidence 0.22) and asserts heteroatom hydrogen bonding drives hydration affinity. Fails if the score rewards compact nonpolar solutes or if polar bins are too sparse to inform the surrogate.

no_feedback.revision_summary: Rewrote every conditions entry as a direct field-to-value object, correcting the previous list-of-pairs format. Kept the source-grounded skill on the signed ESOL length priors and the two highest transfer-weight roles (ring 0.758, branch 0.758), trimming weights slightly and decaying semantic mass faster toward the target-only anchor. Retained the polarity counter-hypothesis, which downweights the low-confidence length role, keeps graded hetero_high/hetero_mid support and the mechanistic hydrocarbon interaction, with a mildly softened halogen penalty. Polarity skill is frozen for deployment.

rules.rationale: Broad hetero_low bin (316 candidates) carries modest polarity without the sparsity that crippled hetero_high rules.
Keeps the source length sign but downweighted, since its confidence is only 0.28.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis downweighting the pure size story: moderate polarity in a well-populated bin plus mild hydrophobic penalties should track hydration. Fails if hydration favors highly polar or purely nonpolar extremes instead of moderate mixed solutes.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across sixteen development seeds the source-grounded size and topology transfer outperformed every polarity-led variant (mean AUC ~74.5 and ~66.8 versus ~53.9 and ~52.7), and both polarity skills relied on the sparse hetero_high bin; the remaining weakness of the size skill was its diluted four-rule set, so the length ladder is restored in full and the low-weight branch rule dropped rather than switching families again.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Deployed skill sharpens the surviving size transfer: the full signed length ladder (short +0.45, mid -0.30, long -0.40) is restored, the ring_token_none rule is strengthened to 0.30, the weak branch rule is removed, and semantic mass starts slightly higher at 0.40 with decay to 0.10 since the semantic signal has been consistently useful. The counter-hypothesis is rebuilt to avoid the repeatedly failing hetero_high condition, instead using the broad hetero_low bin with mild halogen and branching penalties and a low semantic_mass_start so the target-only anchor dominates if it is wrong. Only exact catalog field-value pairs are used and no target outcomes are assumed.
